abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive cancer with a poor survival rate. Publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were analyzed to characterize transcriptional changes across 33 PDAC and three normal pancreas samples. Early-stage samples exhibited greater stromal abundance and were enriched for microenvironmental remodeling, whereas advanced-stage samples showed increased proliferation and cellular plasticity. Chemotherapy-treated tumors demonstrated remodeling enrichment alongside reduced immune activity, suggesting adaptive changes. COMET analysis identified SNCG and LY6D as candidate basal-like tumor markers, supporting molecular subtype as a source of transcriptional heterogeneity. These findings highlight distinct tumor microenvironment characteristics between PDAC subtypes and progression.

title: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Progression Is Associated With Reduced Stromal Organization and Adaptive Tumor Signaling at Single-Cell Resolution
